items.title: Scott Robinson interviewed by Monk Rowe,Chautauqua, New York, September 13, 1997
items.q: maybe they knew Lester Young and they probably knew the name Ben Webster but had never heard him play.

ctx.x: Wow. Were the students, did you try to get the students to play styles like that or was it mostly a listening thing.

No it was a listening, it was a lecture class. It was listening and history, and identifying records, identifying players, stuff like that. It was hard because these people for the most part never heard of Chu Berry or — maybe they knew Lester Young and they probably knew the name Ben Webster but had never heard him play. Really. Tenor players even. So it was kind of a struggle. I had to say listen for this type of sound and this way of turning a phrase around, and then I would quiz them by playing records, to…

I haven’t quite heard it put like that but I know what you’re saying, and some people have echoed that as far as the jazz education and how it trains players — the fact that there’s not all the opportunities to play that there used to be I guess is a little hard to overcome, don’t you think?
